From: Meera Raghavan  
To: Family  
Subject: Re: Our plan for next year

Kiran, thank you for saying all of this plainly. You’re right that you should have been part of the conversation sooner. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, but I should have looped you in then—not let you find out after it was under way. I’m sorry. I don’t want you to feel managed or simply handed a decision that affects all of us.

And I am genuinely thrilled that Amma and Appa are coming. I keep imagining the children with them here, and Amma teaching Anika and Rohan to make rasam on Tuesdays (Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable). But that excitement doesn’t mean your concerns should be brushed aside.

On Appa’s heart: I agree this needs a proper plan. I’ve got a quote for six months’ travel insurance with pre-existing cardiac cover, about £640 each; the agent says it covers the stent. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly and do a video consultation in July. He’s happy to share his notes with me, so we can make sure the plan is based on his advice. Leicester Royal is about 15 minutes from our house, and I know half the cardiology team. I also know visitors shouldn’t assume NHS care will be free, so we’ll check exactly what the insurance covers and what to do in an emergency before they travel.

Amma’s six-week point is fair too. Six months is a long time away from home. The return ticket will be flexible, and she can go home whenever she wants; this isn’t a commitment she has to stick out if she’s unhappy. We’ve finished the annexe at the back: it’s on the ground floor, has no steps, and has its own shower with a grab rail. Still, the practical arrangements don’t answer the bigger question of how Amma will feel, and I want us to keep talking about that.

Ganesh Chaturthi matters. The trip doesn’t have to mean losing time together: Amma and Appa could fly from Leicester to Pune for it in September and finish their visit there, or the Pune family could come to us in August. I’d be very happy to cover your family’s flights for an August visit.

One thing I should have explained: the idea actually came from Appa. When Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video in August, Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” I took that as something he wanted to explore, but I can see I should have brought everyone into the discussion before taking steps on the paperwork.

Could we have a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK time / 9:30pm India time? I’d like us to hear how everyone feels and talk through the dates, the health plan and Ganesh Chaturthi together—without treating any of it as settled beyond discussion. Love you all, and I’m glad you raised this.
